observations.text: Reviews across the 5 interport hubs show strong scores on payroll reliability (4.7/5) and modern Euro-6 fleet safety (4.5/5), but high rating variance across locations (Verona/Milan at 4.3/5 vs.
Bologna/Naples at 3.1/5 due to slow candidate response and local warehouse onboarding friction).
Local hub reviews are tracked manually in spreadsheets.

Career portal receives 14,000 monthly visits (82% from smartphones), but 63% of visitors drop off before completing the application form because it requires desktop-style account registration and a 5-page CV upload.

Job descriptions use generic corporate HQ templates that omit C-CQC route allowances, home-time predictability, and fleet specs.
Job descriptions use generic corporate HQ templates that omit C-CQC route allowances, home-time predictability, and fleet specs.
Corporate LinkedIn page reaches white-collar freight clients and HQ analysts well, but has near-zero reach among licensed C-CQC drivers and interport warehouse operators.

The acute bottleneck is exclusively on the 120 frontline C-CQC driver and warehouse operator openings across the regional hubs—especially Bologna and Naples—where average Time-to-Hire has reached 43 days.
Because of the 43-day Time-to-Hire, Operations is burning €190k/quarter on emergency temporary staffing agencies.
The 3-person central HR team wastes over 110 hours/year manually copying hub reviews into Excel and lacks a unified ROI dashboard for the Board.
